{{langnf|ru-latn|'''Kuznyechik'''|Grasshopper|paren=left}}; Cyrillic script: Кузнечик) is a symmetric [[block cipher]]. It has a block size of 128 bits and key length of 256 bits. It is defined in the National Standard of the Russian Federation '''GOST R 34.12-2015'''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gostperevod.com/gost-r-34-12-2015.html |title=GOST R 34.12-2015 |date= |website=GostPerevod}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://tc26.ru/en/standard/gost/GOST_R_34_12_2015_ENG.pdf |title=National Standard of the Russian Federation GOST R 34.12–2015 |website=tc26.ru |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104181913/http://tc26.ru/en/standard/gost/GOST_R_34_12_2015_ENG.pdf |archive-date=2017-11-04 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and also in RFC 7801. It has received scrutiny for the structure of its [[S-box]]es, which the authors claim were randomly generated.

The name of the cipher can be translated from Russian as [[grasshopper]], however, the standard explicitly says that the English name for the cipher is ''Kuznyechik'' ({{IPAc-en|k|ʊ|z|ˈ|n|ɛ|tʃ|ɪ|k|}}). The designers claim that by naming the cipher Kuznyechik they follow the trend of difficult to pronounce algorithm names set up by [[Rijndael]] and [[Keccak]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mjos.fi/doc/rus/gh_ctcrypt.pdf |title=Low-Weight and Hi-End: Draft Russian Encryption Standard |website=Markku-Juhani O. Saarine |access-date=2016-04-15 |archive-date=2016-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428113420/https://mjos.fi/doc/rus/gh_ctcrypt.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> There is also a rumor that the cipher was named after its creators: A. S. Kuzmin,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/69696703_A_S_Kuzmin |title=A. S. Kuzmin's research while affiliated with Lomonosov Moscow State University and other places |website=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref> A. A. Nechaev<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/A_Nechaev |title=Profile: A. A. Nechaev |website=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref> and Company (Russian: '''Куз'''ьмин, '''Неч'''аев '''и''' '''К'''омпания).{{Citation needed|date=October 2020}}<!-- Source of the rumour? -->

The standard '''GOST R 34.12-2015''' defines the new cipher in addition to the old [[GOST block cipher]] (now called Magma) as one and does not declare the old cipher obsolete.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.itsec.ru/articles2/crypto/gost-r-chego-ozhidat-ot-novogo-standarta |title=GOST R 34.12–2015: what to expect from a new standard? |language=Russian |website=itsec.ru}}</ref>

Kuznyechik is based on a [[substitution–permutation network]], though the [[key schedule]] employs a [[Feistel network]].

== Designations ==
'''<math>\mathbb F</math>''' — [[Finite field]] <math>GF(2^8)</math>  <math>x^8 + x^7 + x^6 + x + 1</math>.

'''<math>Bin_8 : \Z_p \rightarrow V_8</math>''' —  <math>\Z_p</math> (<math>p=2^8</math>)

'''<math>{Bin_8}^{-1}: V_8 \rightarrow \Z_p</math>''' —  <math>Bin_8</math>.

'''<math>\delta: V_8 \rightarrow \mathbb F</math>''' —  <math>\mathbb F</math>.

'''<math>\delta^{-1}: \mathbb F \rightarrow V_8</math>''' —  <math>\delta</math>

== Description ==

For encryption, decryption and key generation, the following functions:

<math>Add_2[k](a)=k\oplus a</math>, where <math>k</math>, <math>a</math> are binary strings of the form <math>a=a_{15}||</math>...<math>||a_{0}</math> (<math>||</math> is string [[concatenation]]).

<math>N(a)=S(a_{15})||</math>...<math>||S(a_{0}).~~N^{-1}(a)</math> is a reversed transformation of <math>N(a)</math>.

<math>G(a)=\gamma(a_{15},</math>...<math>,a_0)||a_{15}||</math>...<math>||a_{1}.</math>

<math>G^{-1}(a)</math> — reversed transformation of <math>G(a)</math> , <math>G^{-1}(a)=a_{14}||a_{13}||</math>...<math>||a_{0}||\gamma(a_{14},a_{13},</math>...<math>,a_0,a_{15}).</math>

<math>H(a)=G^{16}(a)</math>, where <math>G^{16}</math> — composition of transformations <math>G^{15}</math> and <math>G</math> etc.

<math>F[k](a_1,a_0)=(HNAdd_2[k](a_1)\oplus a_0, a_1).</math>

=== The nonlinear transformation ===

Non-linear transformation is given by substituting <big>S = Bin<sub>8</sub> S' Bin<sub>8</sub><sup>−1</sup>.</big>

Values of the substitution <big>S'</big> are given as array <big>S' = (S'(0), S'(1), ..., S'(255))</big>:

<math>S' = (252, 238, 221, 17, 207, 110, 49, 22, 251, 196, 250, 218, 35, 197, 4, 77, 233,</math>
<math>119, 240, 219, 147, 46, 153, 186, 23, 54, 241, 187, 20, 205, 95, 193, 249, 24, 101,</math>
<math>90, 226, 92, 239, 33, 129, 28, 60, 66, 139, 1, 142, 79, 5, 132, 2, 174, 227, 106, 143,</math>
<math>160, 6, 11, 237, 152, 127, 212, 211, 31, 235, 52, 44, 81, 234, 200, 72, 171, 242, 42,</math>
<math>104, 162, 253, 58, 206, 204, 181, 112, 14, 86, 8, 12, 118, 18, 191, 114, 19, 71, 156,</math><math>
</math><math>183, 93, 135, 21, 161, 150, 41, 16, 123, 154, 199, 243, 145, 120, 111, 157, 158, 178,</math>
<math>177, 50, 117, 25, 61, 255, 53, 138, 126, 109, 84, 198, 128, 195, 189, 13, 87, 223,</math>
<math>245, 36, 169, 62, 168, 67, 201, 215, 121, 214, 246, 124, 34, 185, 3, 224, 15, 236,</math>
<math>222, 122, 148, 176, 188, 220, 232, 40, 80, 78, 51, 10, 74, 167, 151, 96, 115, 30, 0,</math>
<math>98, 68, 26, 184, 56, 130, 100, 159, 38, 65, 173, 69, 70, 146, 39, 94, 85, 47, 140, 163,</math>
<math>165, 125, 105, 213, 149, 59, 7, 88, 179, 64, 134, 172, 29, 247, 48, 55, 107, 228, 136,</math>
<math>217, 231, 137, 225, 27, 131, 73, 76, 63, 248, 254, 141, 83, 170, 144, 202, 216, 133,</math>
<math>97, 32, 113, 103, 164, 45, 43, 9, 91, 203, 155, 37, 208, 190, 229, 108, 82, 89, 166,</math>
<math>116, 210, 230, 244, 180, 192, 209, 102, 175, 194, 57, 75, 99, 182).</math>

=== Linear transformation ===

<math>\gamma</math>:
<math>\gamma(a_{15}, </math>...<math>, a_0) = \delta^{-1}~(148 * \delta(a_{15}) + 32 * \delta(a_{14}) + 133 * \delta(a_{13}) + 16 * \delta(a_{12}) +</math>
<math>194 * \delta(a_{11}) + 192 * \delta(a_{10}) + 1 * \delta(a_9) + 251 * \delta(a_8) + 1 * \delta(a_7) + 192 * \delta(a_6) +</math>
<math>194 * \delta(a_5) + 16 * \delta(a_4) + 133 * \delta(a_3) + 32 * \delta(a_2) + 148 * \delta(a_1) + 1 * \delta(a_0)),</math>

operations of addition and multiplication are carried out in the field <math>\mathbb F</math>.

=== Key generation ===

The key generation algorithm uses iterative constant <math>C_i=H(Bin_{128}(i))</math><big>, i=1,2,...32</big>
and sets the shared key as follows: <math>K=k_{255}||</math>...<math>||k_0</math>.

Iterated keys:

<math>K_1=k_{255}||</math>...<math>||k_{128}</math>

<math>K_2=k_{127}||</math>...<math>||k_{0}</math>

<math>(K_{2i+1}, K_{2i+2})=F[C_{8(i-1)+8}]</math>...<math>F[C_{8(i-1)+1}](K_{2i-1}, K_{2i}), i=1, 2, 3, 4.</math>

=== Encryption algorithm ===

<math>E(a)=Add_2[K_{10}]HNAdd_2[K_9]</math>...<math>HNAdd_2[K_2]HNAdd_2[K_1](a),</math> where a — 128-bit string.

=== Decryption algorithm ===

<math>D(a)=Add_2[K_{1}]N^{-1}H^{-1}Add_2[K_2]</math>...<math>N^{-1}H^{-1}Add_2[K_9]N^{-1}H^{-1}Add_2[K_{10}](a).</math>

==Cryptanalysis==
Riham AlTawy and Amr M. Youssef describe a [[meet-in-the-middle attack]] on the 5-round reduced Kuznyechik which enables recovery of the key with a [[time complexity]] of 2<sup>140</sup>, [[memory complexity]] of 2<sup>153</sup>, and data complexity of 2<sup>113</sup>.<ref name="mitm">{{cite journal |author1=Riham AlTawy |author2=Amr M. Youssef |date=2015-04-17 |title=A Meet in the Middle Attack on Reduced Round Kuznyechik |journal=IEICE Transactions on Fundamentals of Electronics, Communications and Computer Sciences |volume=98 |issue=10 |page=2194 |doi=10.1587/transfun.E98.A.2194 |bibcode=2015IEITF..98.2194A |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/096.pdf }}</ref>

[[Alex Biryukov]], Leo Perrin, and Aleksei Udovenko published a paper in which they show that the [[S-box]]es of Kuznyechik and [[Streebog]] were not created [[pseudo-random]]ly but by using a hidden algorithm which they were able to [[reverse engineer]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=[[Alex Biryukov]] |author2=Leo Perrin |author3=Aleksei Udovenko |date=2016-02-18 |title=Reverse-Engineering the S-box of Streebog, Kuznyechik and STRIBOBr1 (Full Version) |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/071.pdf }}</ref>

Later Leo Perrin and Aleksei Udovenko published two alternative decompositions of the S-box and proved its connection to the S-box of the Belarusian cipher BelT.<ref>{{cite web
| author=Léo Perrin, Aleksei Udovenko
| title=Exponential S-boxes: a Link Between the S-boxes of BelT and Kuznyechik/Streebog
| year=2017
| url=https://tosc.iacr.org/index.php/ToSC/article/view/567
| access-date=2017-02-03
}}</ref> The authors of the paper note that while the reason for using such a structure remains unclear, generating S-boxes by a hidden algorithm contradicts the concept of [[nothing-up-my-sleeve number]]s which could prove that no weaknesses were intentionally introduced in their design.

Riham AlTawy, Onur Duman, and Amr M. Youssef published two [[fault attack]]s on Kuznyechik which show the importance of protecting the implementations of the cipher.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=Riham AlTawy |author2=Onur Duman |author3=Amr M. Youssef |date=2015-04-17 |title=Fault Analysis of Kuznyechik |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/347.pdf }}</ref>

== Adoption ==
[[VeraCrypt]] (a fork of [[TrueCrypt]]) included Kuznyechik as one of its supported encryption algorithms.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.veracrypt.fr/en/Kuznyechik.html |title=Kuznyechik |work=VeraCrypt Documentation |publisher=IDRIX |access-date=2018-02-03}}</ref>
